name: Vanthorpe Spire Restraint Ankle Monitor (Court-Issue)
description:
Matte graphite polymer shell over a titanium locking core, 6cm tall, contoured to sit above the ankle bone. The Vanthorpe corponation crest is embossed subtly on the outer face — small enough to read only up close, large enough to know it's there. Surface finish is deliberately utilitarian, a quiet corporate message that this is infrastructure, not fashion.

A single amber LED pulses every 8 seconds during normal operation, shifting to red if tamper protocols trigger. Worn by court-processed individuals as a condition of provisional movement within designated GLMZ zones.
functionality: Continuous GPS broadcast to GLMZ judicial oversight network, tamper detection with 30-second alert window, biometric contact monitoring for removal detection, zone-boundary alerts. Certified for digitigrade limb fitting with extended shell variants available on request.
what_it_says: The city knows exactly where you are, and it wants everyone else to know that it knows.
worn_by: Tier 1 residents caught in jurisdictional sweeps
price_range: Φ0 (court-issued) / Φ2,200 (black market removal attempt tools — rarely successful)
story_hooks: A Tier 3 systems tech claims the firmware has a 4-minute GPS blind spot that cycles every 72 hours — the information is selling for serious Quanta on dark forums.
Vanthorpe's contract to supply court monitors was won over three competitors; the losing bids were each filed by subsidiaries Vanthorpe secretly owns.
Someone has been wearing a dead person's monitor for six weeks without triggering a flag — either the system is broken or someone inside is running cover.
related_entities: Axiom Systems Perception Filter Rounds PFR-1 'Blind Spot'

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, clinical monitoring device that sits prominently above the ankle bone like a corporate seal. The matte graphite finish reads as institutional and inescapable—a constant visual reminder of legal constraint. On a wearer, it catches light subtly but never lets the eye forget it's there.
physical_description.fit: Snug and contoured, sits directly above the ankle bone without gap or slip. The curved polymer shell follows the leg's natural geometry. Designed for 24/7 wear without chafing, though the psychological fit is suffocating.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte graphite polymer shell (scuff-resistant, temperature-regulated) over titanium locking core (tamper-resistant, cannot be cut or bypassed without triggering alert)
physical_description.texture: Smooth polymer exterior with a subtle stippled grip pattern; barely perceptible to touch but visible under raking light. The embossed Vanthorpe crest creates a raised tactile marker—a brand burned into the skin's memory.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte graphite (corporate gray) with amber LED indicator that pulses steadily during normal operation. Red LED activation signals tamper attempt or zone breach.
physical_description.closures: Locking titanium clasps sealed at manufacture—no user-accessible closures. Removal only possible by authorized Vanthorpe technicians or court order.
distinctive_features: Embossed Vanthorpe corporation crest (readable only up close, impossible to ignore)
Single amber LED pulsing every 8 seconds (switches to red on tamper/breach)
Contoured polymer shell that follows ankle bone geometry
Titanium core resistant to cutting, prying, or physical bypass
Subtle stippled grip pattern on polymer surface
Temperature-regulation systems prevent discomfort but ensure constant presence awareness
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 indicator (marks wearer as legally processed, sub-grade civil status, restricted movement rights)
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by court-processed individuals, parolees, and those under provisional freedom conditions. Signals legal entanglement, restricted autonomy, and corporate-judicial control. The Vanthorpe crest is a brand—you belong to the system monitoring you.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on installation, then accumulates micro-scratches, dust in the stippled texture, occasional condensation under the polymer shell. Long-term wear shows darkening around the LED window from repeated activation cycles. Never truly 'worn in'—it remains clinical and foreign.
